title: FULL OUTER JOIN
description: Combine datasets with FULL OUTER JOIN to retain all rows from both tables, reconcile accounting ledgers, and audit discrepancies.

data.text: A **`FULL OUTER JOIN`** returns all rows from both tables. Where rows match, columns are populated together; where either side lacks a match, `NULL` values are returned for the missing side. It is the union of a `LEFT JOIN` and a `RIGHT JOIN`.

data.title: Reconciling Internal Invoices with Stripe Payout Records
data.content: Detects invoices missing in Stripe and Stripe payments missing in internal database.
data.code:
SELECT 
    COALESCE(i.invoice_number, s.stripe_invoice_id) AS reference_id,
    i.amount AS internal_amount,
    s.amount_received AS stripe_amount,
    CASE 
        WHEN i.id IS NULL THEN 'Missing in Internal DB'
        WHEN s.id IS NULL THEN 'Missing in Stripe'
        WHEN i.amount <> s.amount_received THEN 'Amount Mismatch'
        ELSE 'Matched'
    END AS audit_status
FROM internal_invoices i
FULL OUTER JOIN stripe_charges s 
    ON s.stripe_invoice_id = i.invoice_number
WHERE i.amount <> s.amount_received 
   OR i.id IS NULL 
   OR s.id IS NULL;

data.text: Reconciling Two Systems Step by Step

The reconciliation query answers three questions at once: which keys exist on both sides, which exist only in the first table, and which exist only in the second. The `WHERE` clauses turn the full outer join into labelled buckets, and `COALESCE` gives every row a single join key.

data.title: Label every mismatch in one pass
data.content: Each row is tagged with where it came from, so a single result set drives the remediation report.
data.code:
SELECT
    COALESCE(i.invoice_id, p.payment_ref) AS ref,
    i.amount                              AS invoiced_amount,
    p.amount                              AS paid_amount,
    CASE
        WHEN p.payment_ref IS NULL THEN 'missing payment'
        WHEN i.invoice_id IS NULL  THEN 'orphan payment'
        WHEN i.amount <> p.amount  THEN 'amount mismatch'
        ELSE 'matched'
    END AS reconciliation_status
FROM invoices AS i
FULL OUTER JOIN payments AS p
    ON p.payment_ref = i.invoice_id
WHERE i.invoice_id IS NULL
   OR p.payment_ref IS NULL
   OR i.amount <> p.amount
ORDER BY ref;

data.title: Count both sides first
data.text: Run a quick `SELECT COUNT(*)` on each table before the join. If the joined result is larger than either side, you have duplicate keys and the join is fanning out. Reconciliation logic that ignores duplicate keys reports phantom mismatches.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `FULL OUTER JOIN` preserves every row from both tables.
Use `COALESCE(a.key, b.key)` to produce a unified identifier.
Ideal for auditing, data migrations, and financial reconciliations.
